chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿImrān ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿImrān al-Qummī, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said: A man goes out hunting for the distance of one day or two days; should he shorten or complete? He said: If he goes out for his own sustenance and the sustenance of his dependents, then let him shorten. But if he goes out seeking excess, then no, and no honor.

key_terms.الصَّيْدِ: hunting as the purpose of travel
key_terms.عِيَالِهِ: his dependents or family members he supports
key_terms.لِطَلَبِ الْفُضُولِ: for seeking surplus or nonessential gain
key_terms.وَلَا كَرَامَةَ: an expression of disapproval, meaning no concession or privilege
key_terms.يَقْصُرُ: to shorten the salat (prayer) during travel
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: to perform the salat (prayer) in full

ai.seo_question: Does a person traveling for hunting shorten salat (prayer) or perform it in full?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the salat of a hunter who travels. If his journey is for necessary livelihood for himself and his dependents, he shortens the prayer; but if it is for superfluous gain, he does not receive that concession.
